assessment: A small three quarter bath in an older basement, and the honest note is that the reveal is short. Finished footage runs 4:18 to 5:22, about 64 seconds in total, and roughly a third of that is the hallway floor and the louvred furnace closet. There is enough for one Short and no more, and no room to be wasteful with it. The relocated floor drain is the strongest single beat, it is a real problem most homeowners have never thought about, and the payoff is a tiled entry with no drain in the middle of it. No cost talk anywhere in this episode.

project_context.summary: Small basement three quarter bath in an older home. A floor drain sat in the middle of the hallway outside it, so the drain was relocated into the furnace closet, the old one filled and the slab leveled, and the whole entry tiled. Inside, the shower was rebuilt in tile with a glass door and a half wall, on a hex mosaic pan, with a custom vanity built to the space, a quartz top, a medicine cabinet mirror, an elongated comfort height toilet, and a cabinet above it the homeowner chose.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut entirely from 4:18 to 5:23, the finished reveal. No before footage and no progress footage, so nothing that was torn out appears.
notes: Every frame is the finished room.
The episode has no cost segment, so nothing to fence off there.

shorts.full_vo: This little basement three quarter bath in the Happy House is done. Out here in the hallway, the floor used to be painted concrete. With a floor drain sitting right in the middle of it. So we moved that drain into the furnace closet, out of the way. Then filled the old one, leveled the slab, and tiled the whole entry. Inside, the shower is all tile now, with a glass door and a half wall. The shower floor is a hex mosaic in grey and white. The vanity is custom, built to fit the space exactly, with a quartz top. And over the sink, a medicine cabinet mirror. The toilet is elongated and comfort height, like a dining chair. And the cabinet above it is the homeowner's own pick. Small room, and it feels a lot bigger than it did.
